headline: US Embassy warns: Student visas may be revoked for skipping classes
summary: Foreign students in the US may lose their visas and future eligibility if they drop out or leave their programs without notifying their schools.
details: The US Embassy in Dhaka has issued a warning to foreign students studying in the United States regarding the conditions of their student visas.
According to a social media post by the embassy on Saturday, August 22, 2026, students may have their visas revoked if they drop out of their studies or are frequently absent from classes.
The embassy further clarified that leaving a program of study without informing the educational institution can also lead to visa cancellation.
Such violations can result in the loss of eligibility for any future US visas, making it a critical warning for students to maintain their legal status.
Students are advised to always adhere to the visa conditions and maintain a valid legal standing as a student to avoid potential complications.
caption:
Skipping classes in the US could cost you your visa.

The US Embassy in Dhaka has issued a warning to foreign students studying in the United States regarding the conditions of their student visas.

According to a social media post by the embassy on Saturday, August 22, 2026, students may have their visas revoked if they drop out of their studies or are frequently absent from classes.

The embassy further clarified that leaving a program of study without informing the educational institution can also lead to visa cancellation.

Such violations can result in the loss of eligibility for any future US visas, making it a critical warning for students to maintain their legal status.

Students are advised to always adhere to the visa conditions and maintain a valid legal standing as a student to avoid potential complications.

headline_marked: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir [[becomes Bangladesh's 23rd President]]
headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir becomes Bangladesh's 23rd President
summary: Following his assumption of office, the National Parliament Secretariat has declared his parliamentary seat in Thakurgaon-1 vacant.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially assumed office as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. He was previously the elected Member of Parliament for the Thakurgaon-1 constituency.
According to a notification signed by Barrister Md. Golam Sarwar Bhuiyan, Secretary of the Legislative Support Wing of the National Parliament Secretariat, his parliamentary seat is now vacant.
The vacancy was declared in accordance with Article 50(4) of the Constitution, effective from the date he took charge as President on Friday, August 21.
The notification has been sent to the Government Printing Office for publication in an extraordinary issue of the Bangladesh Gazette.
Additionally, a copy of the notification has been forwarded to the Senior Secretary of the Election Commission Secretariat to initiate necessary arrangements for a by-election in the vacant seat.
Following his inauguration, President Mirza Fakhrul paid tribute to the martyrs of the Liberation War at the National Memorial in Savar.
He has also received congratulatory messages from the Presidents of Nepal and the Maldives, while Prime Minister Tarique Ahmed wished him a successful and dignified tenure.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd President of Bangladesh. His parliamentary seat in Thakurgaon-1 has been declared vacant to make way for his new role.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially assumed office as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. He was previously the elected Member of Parliament for the Thakurgaon-1 constituency.

According to a notification signed by Barrister Md. Golam Sarwar Bhuiyan, Secretary of the Legislative Support Wing of the National Parliament Secretariat, his parliamentary seat is now vacant.

The vacancy was declared in accordance with Article 50(4) of the Constitution, effective from the date he took charge as President on Friday, August 21.

The notification has been sent to the Government Printing Office for publication in an extraordinary issue of the Bangladesh Gazette.

Additionally, a copy of the notification has been forwarded to the Senior Secretary of the Election Commission Secretariat to initiate necessary arrangements for a by-election in the vacant seat.

Following his inauguration, President Mirza Fakhrul paid tribute to the martyrs of the Liberation War at the National Memorial in Savar.

He has also received congratulatory messages from the Presidents of Nepal and the Maldives, while Prime Minister Tarique Ahmed wished him a successful and dignified tenure.
